description: earning-health-allslots.sh has a reachable fallback branch for when a trace-derived reason/error string sanitizes down to an empty string, and that branch is completely untested (neither at the pure-core unit level nor at the wiring level). is_fresh_but_barren only requires the RAW cause string to be non-empty (earning-health.py:81: `return bool(only_reason)` on the UNSANITIZED reason/error text) to flag BARREN -- it has no knowledge of sanitize_for_prompt's allowlist. So a real, reachable case exists where a slot's trace writes a non-empty reason/error consisting ENTIRELY of characters outside the sanitizer's allowlist (e.g. a reason string that is only emoji, only CJK/non-ASCII text, or only punctuation like '!!!' or '###') -- is_fresh_but_barren correctly flags this as BARREN (the raw cause is non-empty), but sanitize_for_prompt then reduces it to the empty string, triggering earning-health-allslots.sh:112's `[ -z "$REASON" ] && REASON="unspecified"` fallback (and the analogous SAFE_ID fallback at line 114). Neither test_earning_health.py nor test_earning_health_allslots.sh exercises a reason/error string that survives is_fresh_but_barren's non-empty check but sanitizes to empty -- the self-fix BLOCKER text's 'unspecified' fallback path is dead-in-tests code, unverified to actually produce a sane, non-garbled prompt string end-to-end.

evidence.snippet:
REASON="$(printf '%s' "$RAW_REASON" | python3 "$SELF_DIR/earning-health.py" sanitize-reason 200)"
[ -z "$REASON" ] && REASON="unspecified"
SAFE_ID="$(printf '%s' "$ID" | python3 "$SELF_DIR/earning-health.py" sanitize-reason 80)"
[ -z "$SAFE_ID" ] && SAFE_ID="unspecified-slot"
